title: Part 4 Practice: Basic Concepts of Big Data

questions.text: What is the definition of Big Data according to the module?
options: A) A small collection of data that fits on a single Excel sheet.
B) A blanket term for non-traditional strategies and technologies needed to gather, organize, process, and gather insights from large datasets.
C) A type of database software.
D) Data that is only generated by social media platforms.
questions.correct_answer: B) A blanket term for non-traditional strategies and technologies needed to gather, organize, process, and gather insights from large datasets.
questions.explanation: The module defines: 'Big data is a blanket term for the non-traditional strategies and technologies needed to gather, organize, process, and gather insights from large datasets.'

questions.text: Why is the definition of a 'large dataset' considered to be constantly shifting?
options: A) Because data is always being deleted.
B) Because the scale of big datasets varies significantly from organization to organization and changes with technology.
C) Because there is no way to measure data size.
D) Because data only exists in one fixed size.
questions.correct_answer: B) Because the scale of big datasets varies significantly from organization to organization and changes with technology.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'This means that the common scale of big datasets is constantly shifting and may vary significantly from organization to organization.'

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the 4 Vs of Big Data listed in the module?
options: A) Volume
B) Velocity
C) Variety
D) Value
questions.explanation: The module explicitly lists the 4 Vs as: Volume, Velocity, Variety, and Veracity. 'Value' is often discussed in business contexts, but it is not one of the 4 Vs listed in the module.

questions.text: What does the 'Volume' V of Big Data refer to?
options: A) The speed at which data is generated.
B) The large amounts of data, often measured in Zeta bytes or massive datasets.
C) The different formats of data.
D) The accuracy and trustworthiness of data.
questions.correct_answer: B) The large amounts of data, often measured in Zeta bytes or massive datasets.
questions.explanation: The module defines Volume as: 'large amounts of data Zeta bytes/Massive datasets.'

questions.text: What does the 'Velocity' V of Big Data refer to?
options: A) Data that is static and never changes.
B) Data that is live streaming or in motion, requiring real-time processing.
C) The size of the data in megabytes.
D) The cost of storing the data.
questions.correct_answer: B) Data that is live streaming or in motion, requiring real-time processing.
questions.explanation: The module defines Velocity as: 'Data is live streaming or in motion.'

questions.text: Which V of Big Data refers to the diverse forms of data, including structured, unstructured, and semi-structured?
options: A) Volume
B) Velocity
C) Variety
D) Veracity
questions.explanation: The module defines Variety as: 'data comes in many different forms from diverse sources.' This includes structured, unstructured, and semi-structured data.

questions.text: What is the meaning of the 'Veracity' V of Big Data?
options: A) The variety of data sources.
B) Can we trust the data? How accurate is it? It deals with uncertainty and data quality.
C) The speed of data transmission.
D) The volume of data generated.
questions.correct_answer: B) Can we trust the data? How accurate is it? It deals with uncertainty and data quality.
questions.explanation: The module defines Veracity as: 'can we trust the data? How accurate is it? etc. Uncertainty due to data inconsistency & incompleteness, latency, deception, model approximations.'

questions.text: Why do traditional tools like Excel or standard SQL databases fail to handle Big Data?
options: A) Because they are too expensive.
B) Because they cannot handle the 4 Vs: extreme Volume, fast Velocity, diverse Variety, and Veracity at scale.
C) Because they are not compatible with Microsoft Windows.
D) Because they require too much power to run.
questions.correct_answer: B) Because they cannot handle the 4 Vs: extreme Volume, fast Velocity, diverse Variety, and Veracity at scale.
questions.explanation: The module highlights that Big Data exceeds the computing power or storage of a single computer. Traditional tools crash under Volume, lag behind Velocity, reject Variety, and cannot verify Veracity at scale.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of Velocity in Big Data?
options: A) A historical archive of census data from 1990.
B) Real-time transaction processing at TeleBirr, handling thousands of payments per second.
C) A static Excel file of employee salaries.
D) A printed list of customer names.
questions.correct_answer: B) Real-time transaction processing at TeleBirr, handling thousands of payments per second.
questions.explanation: Velocity refers to data that is live streaming or in motion. TeleBirr processing thousands of real-time transactions is a perfect example of Velocity.

questions.text: How does the concept of 'Variety' in Big Data affect data storage strategies?
options: A) It means all data must be stored in the same format.
B) It means organizations must use flexible storage systems (like NoSQL and data lakes) to handle structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data together.
C) It means only structured data is important.
D) It means data should be stored in physical paper files.
questions.correct_answer: B) It means organizations must use flexible storage systems (like NoSQL and data lakes) to handle structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data together.
questions.explanation: Variety means data comes in many forms. To handle this, organizations cannot rely solely on rigid RDBMS. They must adopt flexible systems like NoSQL databases and data lakes to store and process diverse data types.
